Alex  great to meet you and Chris today, thanks for the thoughtful questions. Recap below + proposed next steps.

Quick recap (what we showed):
- Runtime logging: by default Redwood collects minimal telemetry (request id, model, route, latency, token counts).
- Optional request/response logging: can be enabled per-route; these logs capture request/response payloads and headers for debugging, but we provide configurable redaction and masking before persistent storage.
- Redaction features: built-in PII detectors, configurable regex masks, token-level suppression for high-risk fields, and header scrubbing.
- Data residency & retention: logs are stored in the region linked to the route (you can pin to eu-west-1) and retention is configurable (default 90 days, configurable down to 7 days or up to multi-year for Dedicated/Private).

Answers to your bullets:
- What gets logged by default?
  - Default: request_id, route_id, model_name, latency_ms, token_count, response_status. No request/response bodies or headers are persisted by default.
  - Optional: request/response bodies, request headers, and full trace IDs can be enabled for specific routes (we recommend enabling for short windows and with redaction on).
- Built-in redaction/masking:
  - Standard PII (credit card, SSN, emails, phone numbers) detected and replaceable with configurable masks.
  - Custom regex rules supported; plus ability to drop entire fields before write.
  - Support for partial masking (e.g., keep last 4 digits) or full replacement.
- Data residency:
  - Hosted API: logs persisted in the region of the route; for EU-only requirements we store logs in eu-west-1 and can enforce egress controls.
  - Dedicated/Private: full control  customer-managed storage/KMS and on-prem options.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a short logging controls overview (redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf) that summarizes the options we discussed.
2) Ben (SE)  can you review the questionnaire Alex shared and add a technical appendix for request/response masking and retention defaults?
3) Alex/Chris  would you prefer a short technical call next week to walk through the redaction rules and a sample retention configuration?

Happy to set up a 30-min follow-up.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: FintechCo - logging & redaction controls  internal notes

Marissa  quick internal notes before we sync with Alex & Chris: 

- For request/response logging: our implementation writes to an append-only logging store behind an ingestion service. We perform redaction/masking in the ingestion pipeline before persistence when the route is configured. Important to call out: trace IDs are useful for correlation but can contain PII in some upstream headers; we should recommend scrubbing or hashing trace IDs by default.
- Headers: we maintain a header allowlist/denylist per-route. Sensitive headers (authorization, cookie, x-customer-id) are dropped unless explicitly allowed.
- Retention: Hosted default 90 days; for FintechCo ask we can propose 30 days with the option to increase on Dedicated to satisfy analytics needs.
- Auditability: we can produce an export of logs for a given time window (redacted) for SOC2 reviewers, and we keep an immutable audit trail for config changes.

Action items:
- I'll draft the technical appendix for the questionnaire (include examples of regex rules + sample JSON config for redaction).
- Marissa, get availability for a 30-min technical call next Tue/Wed.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
